This implies a potential regulatory relationship where Ent-Gloeosteretriol is indirectly involved in the activity of Tripartite terminase subunit 3 via the intermediate of Oblonganoside C. The presence of a high confidence score in the interaction between Ent-Gloeosteretriol and ICK, which is a serine/threonine-protein kinase, further supports the notion that Ent-Gloeosteretriol may influence the activity of Tripartite terminase subunit 3 through a kinase-dependent mechanism. The integration of these interactions highlights a possible role for Ent-Gloeosteretriol in modulating the function of Tripartite terminase subunit 3, though the exact nature of this modulation remains to be elucidated.
